primitives.name: Receptor-Effector Connections
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the case of certain other needs, and here lies our chief interest, the situation is remediable only by movement, i.e., muscular activity, on the part of the organism concerned.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that higher organisms possess a nervous system capable of generating motor outputs in response to internal needs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the organism lacks a suitable nervous system or when the need can be satisfied passively.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic state-action value functions (Q-functions) and GSE's sensorimotor contingency matrices, where receptors correspond to environmental states and effectors correspond to actions.
layer2.telemetry: Neural activity in sensory-motor cortex during goal-directed behavior

primitives.name: Primary Reinforcement
primitives.verbatim_quote: The processes of organic evolution have produced a form of nervous system in the higher organisms which, under the conditions of the several needs of this type, will evoke without previous learning a considerable variety of movements each of which has a certain probability of terminating the need.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that reinforcement is an innate property of the organism-environment interaction, independent of prior experience.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the organism cannot associate specific movements with need termination due to environmental complexity or lack of feedback.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's reward signals that drive model-free RL algorithms and GSE's intrinsic motivation modules, where primary reinforcement corresponds to immediate environmental consequences.
layer2.telemetry: Dopamine neuron firing rates during unexpected rewards

primitives.name: Learning Improvement
primitives.verbatim_quote: For the optimal probability of survival of such organisms, inherited behavior tendencies must be supplemented by learning.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that learning enhances the efficiency of receptor-effector mappings beyond what is provided by evolution alone.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the rate of environmental change exceeds the organism's capacity to learn, leading to maladaptation.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's model-based RL where learned environmental dynamics improve long-term planning, and GSE's skill acquisition pipelines where policies are refined through experience.
layer2.telemetry: Performance improvement curves over repeated trials

primitives.name: Casual Observation
primitives.verbatim_quote: That learning does in fact greatly improve the adaptive quality of the behavior of higher organisms is attested by the most casual observation.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that observable behavioral changes are direct evidence of underlying learning processes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when environmental noise obscures the relationship between learning and behavior, or when behavior appears stable despite active learning.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's offline evaluation metrics derived from observational data and GSE's imitation learning frameworks that infer policies from demonstrations.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation coefficients between task performance and training duration
